BURSEVI:v9p274/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p274/r1.speaker: الجنيد
BURSEVI:v9p274/r1.claim: In a report, Hell asks whether God would punish it with anything worse than itself; God answers that His greater fire of love dwells in the hearts of believing friends.
BURSEVI:v9p274/r1.anchor: قال الجنيد قدس سره : قالت النار : يا رب لو لم أطعك هل كنت تعذبني

BURSEVI:v9p274/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p274/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p274/r2.claim: A Persian couplet says love is fire for lovers and burns the seeker’s very being.

BURSEVI:v9p274/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p274/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p274/r3.claim: ‘Glorify by the name of your Lord’ treats glorification as intransitive; the name is mentioned to give thanks for blessings despite deniers, and the preposition indicates means or accompaniment.
BURSEVI:v9p274/r3.anchor: لم يقل فسبح ربك لأن سبح منزل منزلة اللازم

BURSEVI:v9p274/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p274/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v9p274/r4.claim: Ibn Ata says God is too great to be reached by human glorification or to need anything, but honors servants by commanding them to purify themselves through glorifying Him.
BURSEVI:v9p274/r4.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله سبحه أن الله أعظم من أن يلحقه تسبيحك

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p151/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p151/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p151/r1.claim: Section II answers the previously mentioned denial of resurrection and recompense with arguments, in a discourse whose rebuking tone and coherence are clear.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p151/r1.anchor: The succeeding verses discuss the arguments about the Day of Judgement and the reward and punishment which will take place on that day

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p157/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p157/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p157/r2.claim: At the close of the argument, the Prophet should hold his stance and glorify God despite stubborn rejecters, since the arguments support him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p157/r2.anchor: as far as the arguments are concerned, they are in his favour, yet these stubborn people are not budging to accept them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p157/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p157/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p157/r3.claim: God did not create the world merely for people’s luxury or sport; He must bring a day rewarding gratitude and punishing ingratitude.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p157/r3.anchor: It is incumbent upon Him to bring a day in which He rewards the grateful for their gratitude and takes to task the ingrates

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p157/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p157/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p157/r4.claim: The preposition bi in bi-ismi rabbika also expresses seeking help, so the Prophet glorifies God and asks His aid against these circumstances.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p157/r4.anchor: shows that the word here also embraces the meaning of

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p157/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p157/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p157/r5.claim: Name signifies that God's noble attributes are the means of knowing and relating to Him, the source of true knowledge and deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p157/r5.anchor: the only means of a person’s association and relationship with the Almighty are His noble attributes

QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r2.claim: Glorifying the Lord means thinking deeply, diving through the strength of divine unity to find knowledge, and guarding faith from doubts.
QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r2.anchor: اسبح بفكرك في بحار عقلك ، وغص بقوة التوحيد

QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r3.claim: The enumerated signs prepare a path of inference and indicate the need for reflection.
QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r3.anchor: وهذه الآيات التي عدها الله - سبحانه - تمهد لسلوك طريق الاستدلال

BAYDAWI-FULL:56:74-75/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:74-75/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:74-75/r1.claim: Glorify by uttering God’s name or remembering Him; العظيم describes either the name or the Lord. The command responds to blessings by rejecting denial, expressing astonishment at ingratitude, or giving thanks.
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:74-75/r1.anchor: فأحدث التسبيح بذكر اسمه تعالى أو بذكره فإن إطلاق اسم الشيء ذكره

NAHHAS:v4p341/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p341/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p341/r12.claim: The glorification is by remembering God and using His beautiful names.

MUQATIL:56:74-82/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:56:74-82/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:56:74-82/r1.claim: To glorify God's great name means to remember His oneness; He is the greatest.
MUQATIL:56:74-82/r1.anchor: { فسبح } يقول اذكر التوحيد { باسم ربك } يامحمد { العظيم } [آية: 74] يعنى الكبير فلا أكبر منه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:56:71-75/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:56:71-75/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:56:71-75/r3.claim: The command to glorify God declares Him far above what polytheists say.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:56:71-75/r3.anchor: { فسبح باسم ربك العظيم } أي: نزه الله مما يقول المشركون

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p136/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p136/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p136/r1.claim: Verses 49–74 warn Quraysh’s arrogant deniers that continued deviation and rejection of the Prophet will bring the left-hand companions’ fate; self-evident arguments support Judgment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p136/r1.anchor: The arrogant among the Quraysh are addressed and warned that they shall end up with the same fate

ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r26.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r26.speaker: author
ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r26.claim: The response is to glorify the great Lord as exalted above partners and imperfection, by saying Subḥāna rabbiyal-ʿaẓīm or praying.
ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r26.anchor: nâm-ı azametini tenzih ederek tesbih eyle yahut namaz kıl.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r13.claim: Because azim is usually taken as an adjective of “Lord,” the author prefers “glorify the name of your mighty Lord.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r13.anchor: 74. âyetteki azîm kelimesi genellikle “rab” kelimesinin sıfatı kabul edildiği için meâlde “Öyleyse ulu rabbinin adını tesbih et” anlamı tercih edilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r14.claim: Alternatively, azim can modify “name,” yielding “glorify your Lord by His mighty name.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r14.anchor: fakat bunu “isim” kelimesinin sıfatı olarak da düşünmek mümkündür; buna göre meâl şöyle olur: “Öyleyse rabbini yüce ismiyle tesbih et”

ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r1.claim: The command to glorify follows the enumeration of God’s marvelous works and gifts.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r1.anchor: مرتب على ما عدد من بدائع صنعه عز وجل وودائع نعمه سبحانه وتعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r2.claim: One reading takes the command as beginning glorification, treating a transitive verb as intransitive, but understands beginning as continuing because the Prophet never neglected it.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r2.anchor: والمراد على ما قيل : أحدث التسبيح تنزيلا للفعل المتعدي منزلة اللازم وأريد من إحداثه استمراره لا إيجاده

ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r3.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r3.claim: Al-Tibi objects that this reverses the force of ‘beginning’; the command instead means renewing glorification.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r3.anchor: وتعقبه الطيبي بأن هذا عكس ما يقتضيه لفظ الإحداث فالمراد تجديد التسبيح

ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r4.claim: An implied phrase may mean ‘glorify by mentioning your Lord’s name’; alternatively, ‘name’ figuratively means mention.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r4.anchor: وفي الكلام إضمار أي سبح بذكر اسم ربك أو الاسم مجاز عن الذكرفإن إطلاق الأسم للشيء ذكره

ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r5.claim: The bāʾ may indicate instrument or accompaniment; treating it as transitive, as Abu Hayyan seems to, is wrong.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r5.anchor: والباء للإستعانة أو الملابسة وكونها للتعدية كما هو ظاهر كلام أبي حيان ليس بشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r6.claim: ‘The Great’ may modify either the name or the Lord.

ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r7.claim: One purpose is to declare God beyond what those denying His oneness and rejecting His favors say.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r7.anchor: إما لتنزيهه تعالى عما يقوله الجاحدون لوحدانيته عز وجل الكافرون بنعمه سبحانه مع عظمها وكثرتها

ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r8.claim: Another purpose is gratitude: glorifying and magnifying God after His favors praises the true Benefactor.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r8.anchor: أو للشكر على تلك النعم السابقة لأن تنزيهه تعالى وتعظيمه جل وعلا بعد ذكر نعمه سبحانه مدح عليها فهو للمنعم في الحقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r9.claim: A proposed purpose is amazement at disbelievers’ ingratitude; construing subḥān as a metaphor for astonishment is distant, and Al-Alusi prefers the prior explanations.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151/r9.anchor: وسبحان للتعجب مجازا مشهور فسبح بمعنى تعجب وأصله فقل سبحان الله للتعجب وفيه بعد وما تقدم أظهر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r1.claim: A literal reading needs no ellipsis or metaphor: as God’s essence and attributes must be free of defects, the words used for them deserve freedom from disrespect even more.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r1.anchor: فقد قالوا في قوله تعالى : ( سبح اسم ربك الأعلى ) : كما يجب تنزيه ذاته تعالى وصفاته سبحانه عن النقائص يجب تنزيه الألفاظ الموضوعة لها عن سوء الأدب

ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r2.claim: This symbolic reading only works by omitting the bāʾ or treating it as extra, which is against the apparent wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r2.anchor: وفيه أنه إنما يتأتى لو لم تذكر الباء وجعلها زائدة خلاف الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r3.claim: Some identify the addressee as a particular idolater: since idolaters admit God created them and the heavens and earth, they are told to acknowledge that no other deity shares even His name.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r3.anchor: وكان الكفار إذا طولبوا بالوحدانية قالوا : نحن لا نشرك في المعنى وإنما نتخذ أصناما آلهة وذلك إشراك في الاسم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r4.claim: The proposed particular addressee is like a preacher’s generic ‘O poor man’; a general address is possible, but this interpretation is not required.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r4.anchor: وهو كما ترى نعم احتمال عموم الخطاب مما لا ينكر لكن لا يتعين عليه هذا التقرير

ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r5.claim: The apparent meaning of mentioning the Lord or His name remains the ordinary, familiar one.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r5.anchor: ثم الظاهر أن المراد بذكر الرب أو ذكر اسمه سبحانه على ما تقرر سابقا ما هو المتبادر المعروف

ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r6.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r6.claim: Al-Kashf interprets it as the Prophet’s recitation of Qur’an or this surah, which establishes resurrection, recompense, and ranks, preparing for the following oath.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p151#2/r6.anchor: وفي الكشف إن المراد بذلك تلاوته صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم للقرآن أو لهذه السورة الكريمة المتضمنة لاثبات البعث والجزاء

SULAMI:v2p301#6/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p301#6/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p301#6/r1.claim: Wāsiṭī says to glorify God by His name because the name of a thing is the thing itself, and He is the Great.
SULAMI:v2p301#6/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي : سبحه باسمه فإن اسم الشيء هو الشيء بعينه وهو العظيم

SULAMI:v2p301#6/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p301#6/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p301#6/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭā says God is too great to need or be reached by human glorification; commanding it honors servants by letting them manifest their own act of declaring Him transcendent.
SULAMI:v2p301#6/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : سبحه أن الله هو اعظم من أن يلحقه تسبيحك أو يحتاج إلى شيء منك لكنه شرف عبيده بأن أمرهم أن يسبحوه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r1.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī gives becoming rich and becoming poor as the strongest opposing pair.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān groups the cited signs as matters of creation and the necessities of livelihood, including food, drink, and fire.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r2.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : وهذه الأربعة التي ذكرها الله تعالى ووقفهم عليها من أمر خلقهم وما به قوام عيشهم من المطعوم والمشروب , والنار

BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān treats fire as a major proof of resurrection because it transforms one thing into another and produces something from something.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r3.anchor: والنار من أعظم الدلائل على البعث إذ فيها انتقال من شيء إلى شيء إحداث شيء من شيء

BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r4.speaker: ابن برجان
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r4.claim: Ibn Barjān associates water and earth with the creation of the elements, and air and fire with temperaments and qualities.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r4.anchor: قال ابن برجان : إلا أن الماء والأرض لخلق الأركان , والاخلاق والصفات للهواء والنار

BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r5.claim: After these signs of power and creation, God commands glorification that rejects every imperfection, especially denial of resurrection, and expresses wonder, gratitude, and magnification.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r5.anchor: أوقع التنزيه العظيم عن كل شائبة نقص من ترك البعث وغيره ولا سيما بعد بلوغ هذه الأدلة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r6.speaker: ابن برجان
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r6.claim: Ibn Barjān says the heat of the sun makes hellfire a means for gardens, fruit, crops, and livelihoods in this world.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r6.anchor: قال ابن برجان : جعل منها بحرارة الشمس جنات وثمرات وفواكه وزروع ومعايش

BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r7.claim: Mentioning God's name most firmly honors the named; the Lord specially benefited the Prophet by granting him this supreme clarification.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r7.anchor: ولما كان تعظيم الاسم أقعد في تعظيم المسمى قال : { باسم } أي متلبسا بذكر اسم { ربك }

BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r8.claim: The alif in ism is retained here because the spelling occurs less often than in the basmala, where frequent usage encourages abbreviation.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r8.anchor: وأثبتوا ألف الوصل هنا لأنه لم يكثر دوره كثرته في البسملة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r9.claim: Al-ʿAẓīm fills the whole cosmos with majesty, transcends every defect, and lacks no perfection.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r9.anchor: الذي ملأ الأكوان كلها عظمة , فلا شيء منها إلا وهو مملوء بعظمته

BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r10.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r10.claim: Al-Qushayrī says the enumerated signs prepare a person to reason by inference.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r10.anchor: قال القشيري : وهذه الآيات التي عددها سبحانه تمهيد لسلوك طريق الاستدلال

BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r11.claim: The commentary cites a report that an hour of reflection is better than sixty years of worship; no authority or grading is supplied.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p421/r11.anchor: كما في الخبر ( تفكر ساعة خير من عبادة ستين سنة )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p329/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p329/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p329/r1.claim: “Great” can describe either the Lord, whose every perfection is established, or His name, which is metaphorically great because of its blessing and the greatness of the One named.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p329/r1.anchor: و { العظيم } صالح لأن يجعل وصفا ل { ربك } ، وهو عظيم بمعنى ثبوت جميع الكمال له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p329/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p329/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p329/r2.claim: Calling the name great is a common metaphor, approaching literal usage, because of its blessing and the greatness of its referent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p329/r2.anchor: والاسم عظيم عظمة مجازية ليمنه ولعظمة المسمى به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p150/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p150/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p150/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj links the command to glorify with the preceding proofs of God's unity, power, and favor; it means declaring Him free of what they attribute to Him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p150/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج لما ذكر ما يدل على توحيده وقدرته وإنعامه قال فسبح أي برء الله ونزهه عما يقولون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p150/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p150/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p150/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the phrase as praying in the name of the Lord, beginning the prayer with the takbir.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p150/r2.anchor: وقال الضحاك معناه فصل باسم ربك أي استفتح الصلاة بالتكبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p150/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p150/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p150/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir says to glorify by remembering and naming the Lord.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p150/r3.anchor: وقال ابن جرير سبح بذكر ربك وتسميته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p150/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p150/r4.speaker: قيل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p150/r4.claim: Another view treats the prefixed bāʾ as extra and name as meaning the divine essence, yielding the sense glorify your Lord.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p150/r4.anchor: وقيل الباء زائدة والاسم يكون بمعنى الذات والمعنى فسبح ربك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p543/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p543/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p543/r1.claim: God's power creates contrasting sweet water and, if He willed, bitter salt water, as well as fire; both benefit people in worldly life, while fire warns of the Hereafter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p543/r1.anchor: الذي بقدرته خلق هذه الأشياء المختلفة المتضادة الماء العذب الزلال البارد، ولو شاء لجعله ملحا أجاجا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#6/r1.claim: The command means to declare God free of what does not befit Him, or to glorify Him by remembering His name.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#6/r1.anchor: فنزه ربكعما لا يليق به أيها المستمع المستدل أو أراد بالاسم الذكر أي سبح بذكر ربك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#6/r2.claim: Al-ʿazim may describe the genitive annexed noun, or the noun to which it is annexed.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#6/r3.claim: Another gloss takes the command to be the formula Subhana rabbi al-ʿazim.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#6/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#6/r4.claim: A prophetic report says that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet instructed the believers to say it in bowing.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#6/r4.anchor: وجاء مرفوعا أنه لما نزلت هذه الآية قال أجعلوها في ركوعكم

QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r14.claim: The command to glorify God’s great name repudiates the partners and inability to resurrect that idolaters attribute to Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r14.anchor: أي فنزه الله عما أضافه إليه المشركون من الأنداد، والعجز عن البعث

RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r1.claim: After the deniers reject proofs from creation and provision, the Prophet's task is to perfect knowledge of God and service to Him; Razi links this to 20:130.
RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r1.anchor: أن تكمل في نفسك وهو علمك بربك وعملك لربك

RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r2.speaker: المشهور
RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r2.claim: The common parsing treats “name” as extra; mentioning God's name still intensifies reverence, since the truly exalted are named only with descriptions of greatness.
RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r2.anchor: هو المشهور وهو أن الاسم مقحم ، وعلى هذا الجواب فنقول : فيه فائدة زيادة التعظيم

RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r3.claim: A verb can take its object with or without a preposition when the relation is intermediate in clarity; because tasbih really targets the Lord through the name, the hidden relation permits bāʾ.
RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r3.anchor: إذا كان بينهما جاز الوجهان فنقول : سبحته وسبحت به وشكرته وشكرت له

RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r4.claim: Alternatively, bāʾ is meaningful: idolaters concede God created everything but call idols gods by name, so they must not assign the divine name to anything besides Him; the admonition addresses any hearer.
RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r4.anchor: لما ذكر الأمور وقال : نحن أم أنتم ، فاعترف الكل بأن الأمور من الله

RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r5.claim: Alternatively, the command is to glorify God by naming Him aloud among one's people, describing Him and continuing to preach even if they refuse; a purely inward tasbih would not convey this.
RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r5.anchor: فسبح ربك بذكر اسمه بين قومك واشتغل بالتبليغ

RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r6.claim: Razi also allows taking the phrase as beginning with the name of the Lord, making bāʾ nonredundant.
RAZI-FULL:v29p161/r6.anchor: فسبح مبتدئا باسم ربك العظيم فلا تكون الباء زائدة

RAZI-FULL:v29p161#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p161#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p161#2/r1.claim: Tasbih is inward belief that God is one, without partner, and able rather than incapable of resurrection, or verbal praise such as “Subhan Allah,” or equivalent words.
RAZI-FULL:v29p161#2/r1.anchor: فبأن يعتقد فيه أنه واحد منزه عن

RAZI-FULL:v29p161#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p161#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p161#2/r2.claim: Real divine unity excludes body, accident, location, and being in, on, or from anything; affirming God's power entails knowledge, will, life, and other attributes, discussed further in al-Ikhlas.
RAZI-FULL:v29p161#2/r2.anchor: لزم أن لا يكون جسما لأن الجسم فيه أشياء كثيرة وهو واحد حقيقي لا كثرة لذاته

RAZI-FULL:v29p161#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p161#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p161#2/r3.claim: Razi distinguishes the epithets: perceptible greatness suggests nearness to all, while absolute elevation suggests remoteness from everything; God transcends perception, and positive attributes exceed what knowledge reaches.
RAZI-FULL:v29p161#2/r3.anchor: أما الفرق بين العظيم والأعلى فهو أن العظيم يدل على القرب ، والأعلى يدل على البعد

RAZI-FULL:v29p161#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p161#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p161#2/r4.claim: “Higher” directly conveys transcendence, while “greater” combines an affirmative notion with a negative one; Razi therefore judges “al-Aʿlā” the more apt usage.
RAZI-FULL:v29p161#2/r4.anchor: فالأعلى مستعمل على حقيقته لفظا ومعنى ، والأعظم مستعمل على حقيقته لفظا

STUDYQURAN:56:74/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:74/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:56:74/r1.claim: This is one of many verses enjoining human beings to glorify God.
STUDYQURAN:56:74/r1.anchor: This is one of many verses in which human beings are enjoined to glorify God.

STUDYQURAN:56:74/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:74/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:56:74/r2.claim: The command can also mean glorifying by God's Name, thus commanding invocation of the Name.
STUDYQURAN:56:74/r2.anchor: It can also mean, “Glorify by the Name of thy Lord,” thus indicating a command to invoke the Name of God.

STUDYQURAN:56:74/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:74/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:56:74/r3.claim: Tasbīḥ means declaring something transcendent beyond everything else.
STUDYQURAN:56:74/r3.anchor: The term for “glorification,”tasbīḥ, indicates declaring something transcendent beyond all else.

STUDYQURAN:56:74/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:74/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:56:74/r4.claim: Though God is responsible for the matters in 56:58–73, He transcends them: He performs many other tasks and their perceived deficiencies cannot be attributed to Him.
STUDYQURAN:56:74/r4.anchor: although God is responsible for all of the things mentioned in vv. 58–73, He is completely beyond them

STUDYQURAN:56:74/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:74/r5.speaker: Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:56:74/r5.claim: Bḍ allows “the Magnificent” to modify either “Name” or “Lord.”
STUDYQURAN:56:74/r5.anchor: The Magnificent can be taken to modify either Name or Lord (Bḍ).

STUDYQURAN:56:74/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:74/r6.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:56:74/r6.claim: Aj also reads the verse as a command to glorify God, whose Glory exceeds anything anyone can say of it.
STUDYQURAN:56:74/r6.anchor: This verse can also be seen as a command to glorify God, since God’s Glory is beyond what anyone else can say of it (Aj).

TABATABAI:56:63-74/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r1.claim: After creation and allotted death as preparation for resurrection and recompense, God cites crops, water, and fire, the three chief necessities of worldly life, to establish His lordship as governance rooted in ownership.
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r1.anchor: عد لهم أمورا ثلاثة من أهم ما يعيشون به في الدنيا وهي الزرع الذي يقتاتون به والماء الذي يشربونه

TABATABAI:56:63-74/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r10.claim: The command addresses the Prophet after signs of lordship and the deniers' rejection of resurrection; it turns from them as uncomprehending and orders glorification against their shirk and denial of recompense.
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r10.anchor: خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. لما ذكر سبحانه شواهد ربوبيته لهم

TABATABAI:56:63-74/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r11.claim: The fa makes glorification follow the preceding proof; bi can mean using the Lord's name or being associated with it, and bism can mean remembrance because naming something mentions it.
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r11.anchor: الفاء لتفريع التسبيح على ما تقدم من البيان، والباء للاستعانة أو الملابسة

TABATABAI:56:63-74/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r12.claim: Alternatively, bi is transitive: to sanctify the Lord's name is to sanctify the Lord, meaning purify His name from association or denial of resurrection and recompense.
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r12.anchor: أو الباء للتعدية لأن تنزيه اسم الشيء تنزيه له، والمعنى نزه اسم ربك من أن تذكر له شريكا أو تنفي عنه البعث والجزاء

TABATABAI:56:63-74/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r13.claim: Al-ʿAzim can grammatically describe either the Lord or His name.

TABRISI:56:65-74/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:56:65-74/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:56:65-74/r18.claim: After recalling God’s signs of oneness and favors, the command means to declare God free of what people wrongly attribute to Him and to purify Him of unfit descriptions.
TABRISI:56:65-74/r18.anchor: { فسبح باسم ربك العظيم } أي فبرئ الله تعالى مما يقولونه في وصفه ونزهه عما لا يليق بصفاة.

TABRISI:56:65-74/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:56:65-74/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:56:65-74/r19.claim: Another interpretation is to say “Glory be to my Lord, the Mighty”; the Prophet instructed that this be said in bowing.
TABRISI:56:65-74/r19.anchor: قل سبحان ربي العظيم فقد صح عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه لما نزلت هذه الآية قال:

TABRISI:56:57-74/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:56:57-74/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:56:57-74/r1.claim: When the verse was revealed, the Prophet instructed worshippers to say it during bowing.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p256/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p256/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p256/r1.claim: Glorifying God here means declaring him free of what people say in describing him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p256/r1.anchor: أي فبرئ الله عز وجل مما يقولون في وصفه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r10.claim: After the proofs of divine power, resurrection examples, and embedded blessings, God directs the Messenger to a distinctive glorification as a fresh recollection of divine majesty and gratitude.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r10.anchor: رتب على ما مضى من الكلام المشتمل على دلائل عظمة القدرة الإلهية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r11.claim: Even though the Messenger continually glorifies God, renewed reflection gives each state of worship distinct merits and greater reward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r11.anchor: فالرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يخلو عن تسبيح ربه والتفكر في عظمة شأنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r17.claim: After citing these signs, God commands the Prophet to glorify his Lord and clear His exalted names of what the unbelievers say.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r17.anchor: ثم أمر نبيه بتنزيه ربه تعالى وتبرئة أسمائه العلى عما يقوله الكفرة الذين حجوا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r8.claim: The command may mean begin glorifying by uttering God's name, or “name” may mean remembrance, so glorify by remembering your Lord.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r8.anchor: فأحدث التسبيح بذكر اسم ربك ، أو أراد بالاسم : الذكر ، أي : بذكر ربك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r9.claim: Al-ʿaẓīm can grammatically modify either the annexed noun or its genitive complement.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r10.claim: Given the signs of God's power and favor, glorify Him by saying subḥān Allāh: to reject deniers' claims, marvel at their ingratitude, or thank Him for the listed blessings.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r10.anchor: لما ذكر ما دل على قدرته وإنعامه على عباده قال : فأحدث التسبيح وهو أن يقول : سبحان الله ، إما تنزيها له عما يقول الظالمون
